title: Cohesin prevents local mixing of condensed euchromatic domains in living human cells.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed from GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE318385: GSM9493575 and GSM9493577 ATAC-seq (assay for transposase-accessible chromatin) peak files (63,346 and 67,398 peaks, 10-column narrowPeak) and the consensus region file GSE318385_HCT116_WT_concensus.gtf.gz (61,779 peak records, 24 chromosomes). Read the GEO file listing: 6 samples, 3 untreated + 3 cohesin-depleted (5-Ph-IAA), each with a 84-103 MB bigwig coverage track plus peaks; no count matrix and no differential-accessibility table anywhere in the series. Downloaded both Zenodo deposits (10.5281/zenodo.16959115, 10.5281/zenodo.18404051) and listed their contents: these are analysis scripts only, except one example trajectory file data01.txt (4,205 tracks, 118,352 localizations, columns particle_id/frame/x/y, median track length 21 frames, no condition label).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the imaging experiments comprise ~15-30 cells per condition and ~820,000 displacement angles per condition; the DDBJ BioProjects (PRJDB17378, PRJDB17380, PRJDB39674) hold only raw pulldown sequencing reads, which project rules forbid downloading. Nature's per-figure 'Source Data' files could not be retrieved: the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice and the PMC open-access package service returned 404, so their contents are unverified.

a1_downloadable.note: For the ATAC-seq route, yes: peak files and bigwigs download anonymously from GEO without login (I pulled two peak files and the consensus GTF). For the paper's core imaging route, no: single-nucleosome trajectories and 3D structured-illumination images are not deposited in any repository, only one unlabelled 4,205-track example file bundled inside the code archive.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAILS. The only plausible label, 'how much does this region's accessibility change when cohesin is removed', exists nowhere as a column: GEO holds 6 bigwig coverage tracks and per-sample peak calls, with no count matrix and no differential-accessibility result. The label would have to be built by quantifying signal over 61,779 consensus peaks in six coverage tracks and running a 3-versus-3 replicate test, i.e. constructed, not read off.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed further after A2 failed. For the record: only genomic coordinates are given; DNA sequence inputs would require a separate hg38 genome download, and the imaging inputs (movies, trajectories) are absent.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed further after A2 failed. narrowPeak columns follow the documented MACS2 standard (fold-enrichment, -log10 p and q); the example trajectory file is in camera pixels with a 65 nm pixel size stated in the code README, not in the file.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessed further after A2 failed. 61,779 consensus peaks sounds ample, but the real unit of replication is 3 untreated versus 3 depleted libraries from one cell line in one lab; for the imaging route the unit is 15-30 cells per condition, far under the 400-row classification floor.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.6 GB (six bigwig tracks at 84-103 MB each plus peak files)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessed further after A2 failed. Individual bigwigs exceed the project's 50 MB per-file cap and would need it raised deliberately, but the total fits a 16 GB laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO sample titles and treatments (3 non-treated, 3 5-Ph-IAA) match the paper's ATAC-seq description; no peak counts are quoted in the paper to contradict the 61,779 I counted.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed further after A2 failed. Worth recording: the paper's four nucleosome 'subpopulations' (superslow/slow/fast/superfast) are outputs of the authors' own Richardson-Lucy deconvolution plus Gaussian-mixture fit, so training on them would distil their pipeline rather than measure biology - a textbook A8 circularity failure.

existing_models.name: DeepSPT, a deep-learning framework for temporal analysis of single-particle tracking trajectories (Nature Methods 2025, doi 10.1038/s41592-025-02665-8)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors to segment and classify diffusive behaviour (normal, directed, confined, subdiffusive) and to distinguish chromatin compartments from H2B trajectory dynamics; exact numbers and split not retrieved, only the abstract-level description from search results.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I only saw search summaries, not the discussion.

existing_models.name: AnDi Challenge methods, the community benchmark for inferring diffusion mode and anomalous exponent from single trajectories (Nature Communications 2021, doi 10.1038/s41467-021-26320-w)
existing_models.score_and_split: Thirteen teams benchmarked on simulated trajectories; the top four methods in each dimensionality were all machine-learning based and clustered in performance. Numbers not retrieved beyond this summary.

backbone.name: none applicable - no sequence, molecule or single-cell input survives Part A

integration.partner_dataset: ENCODE HCT116 ATAC-seq and the published RAD21-degron Hi-C/ATAC data of Rao et al. 2017 (same HCT116 RAD21-AID system)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does cohesin loss change DNA accessibility anywhere reproducibly, and is that change predictable from sequence - a question these 6 libraries alone cannot answer at the depth already published.

controls.positive_control: Would have been: recover the known enrichment of ATAC peaks at promoters and CTCF motifs; recover the published result that global accessibility barely changes after cohesin loss.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling across peaks, and swapping replicate labels within condition.
controls.external_validation: Rao et al. 2017 HCT116 RAD21-degron ATAC-seq, same cell line and degron system, independently produced.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built here could only claim: 'in one colorectal cancer cell line, in one lab, with three libraries per condition, sequence features associate with a difference in transposase accessibility that the literature says is close to zero' - which is a claim about noise, not biology.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence at accessible regions to predict which ones change accessibility when the cohesin ring is removed.
plain_idea.train_on: One 1-kilobase DNA sequence per accessible region, for the 61,779 consensus regions I counted in the deposited peak file, plus simple features such as distance to the nearest gene start.
plain_idea.predict: The change in transposase-accessible signal between cohesin-depleted and untreated cells. The true answer would come from ATAC-seq (assay for transposase-accessible chromatin) read coverage in 3 treated versus 3 untreated libraries - but no such change value is deposited; it would have to be computed from the six coverage tracks.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome-organisation labs argue about whether loop extrusion by cohesin controls local accessibility; a sequence model that predicted which sites respond would point to the DNA features that matter. As it stands the experiment is too small and the known effect too near-zero for that to be learnable.

more_or_better_data.why: Six ATAC-seq libraries from one cell line is far less than what sequence-to-accessibility models already train on (ENCODE-scale, hundreds of cell types), and the cohesin-degron ATAC comparison was already published by Rao et al. 2017 in the same HCT116 system.

confidence_score.why: Three replicates per condition do allow a per-region noise estimate, but with n=3 the uncertainty on each region's change is large and would dominate the signal.

models_beatable.why: The relevant incumbents for trajectory analysis (DeepSPT, 2025) and for sequence-to-accessibility (Enformer-class models) are recent, and the trajectory data needed to compete with the former is not deposited at all.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model can be run as a baseline on this exact label because the label does not exist in the deposit; the condition 'our model sees everything the baseline sees plus new data' cannot be met.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: (1) classify single-nucleosome trajectories by cohesin status, or predict diffusion state from track shape - blocked because the trajectories are not deposited (one unlabelled 4,205-track example file sits inside the code archive) and because the paper's state labels are its own deconvolution pipeline's output (A8 circularity); (2) predict from DNA sequence which accessible regions lose accessibility on cohesin depletion - blocked because no differential-accessibility table exists, only six bigwig coverage tracks and per-sample peak calls, and the published effect size in this system is near zero.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: quantifying six 84-103 MB bigwigs over 61,779 peaks needs a bigwig reader that is not in the allowed dependency list, plus an hg38 download for sequence, which is why the feature table alone is roughly two days rather than two hours.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask GEO for a differential-accessibility or count table - there is none, only coverage tracks and peak calls; that single listing check (one minute) kills the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A2. The paper's core measurement - single-nucleosome trajectories and super-resolution images of euchromatin domains - is not deposited anywhere (I found only one unlabelled example trajectory file of 4,205 tracks inside the Zenodo code archive, and no imaging repository accession). The only modellable deposit is six ATAC-seq libraries from one cell line with no count matrix and no differential-accessibility column, so the prediction target would have to be constructed from coverage tracks, for an effect the literature reports as close to zero. Secondary failures: A8 (the paper's motion-state labels are its own deconvolution pipeline's output) and A5 at the true unit of replication (3 libraries or ~30 cells per condition).
